verses.original: Ἐν ἐκείνῳ τῷ καιρῷ ἤκουσεν Ἡρῴδης ὁ τετραάρχης τὴν ἀκοὴν Ἰησοῦ
verses.transliteration: En ekeinō tō kairō ēkousen Hērōdēs ho tetraarchēs tēn akoēn Iēsou
verses.literal: At that time Herod the tetrarch heard the reports about Jesus
verses.literalPt: NAQUELE tempo ouviu Herodes, o tetrarca, a fama de Jesus,

verses.original: καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς παισὶν αὐτοῦ Οὗτός ἐστιν Ἰωάννης ὁ Βαπτιστής αὐτὸς ἠγέρθη ἀπὸ τῶν νεκρῶν καὶ διὰ τοῦτο αἱ δυνάμεις ἐνεργοῦσιν ἐν αὐτῷ
verses.transliteration: kai eipen tois paisin autou Houtos estin Iōannēs ho Baptistēs autos ēgerthē apo tōn nekrōn kai dia touto hai dynameis energousin en autō
verses.literal: and said to his servants This is John the Baptist he has risen from the dead That is why miraculous powers are at work in him
verses.literalPt: E disse aos seus criados: Este é João o Batista; ressuscitou dos mortos, e por isso estas maravilhas operam nele.

verses.original: Ὁ γὰρ Ἡρῴδης κρατήσας τὸν Ἰωάνην ἔδησεν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐν φυλακῇ ἀπέθετο διὰ Ἡρῳδιάδα τὴν γυναῖκα Φιλίππου τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ αὐτοῦ
verses.transliteration: Ho gar Hērōdēs kratēsas ton Iōanēn edēsen auton kai en phylakē apetheto dia Hērōdiada tēn gynaika Philippou tou adelphou autou
verses.literal: Now Herod had arrested John and bound him and put him in prison on account of Herodias his brother Philip’s wife
verses.literalPt: Porque Herodes tinha prendido João, e tinha-o maniatado e encerrado no cárcere, por causa de Herodias, mulher de seu irmão Filipe;

verses.original: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ὁ Ἰωάννης αὐτῷ Οὐκ ἔξεστίν σοι ἔχειν αὐτήν
verses.transliteration: elegen gar ho Iōannēs autō Ouk exestin soi echein autēn
verses.literal: because John had been telling him It is not lawful for you to have her
verses.literalPt: Porque João lhe dissera: Não te é lícito possuí-la.

verses.original: καὶ θέλων αὐτὸν ἀποκτεῖναι ἐφοβήθη τὸν ὄχλον ὅτι ὡς προφήτην αὐτὸν εἶχον
verses.transliteration: kai thelōn auton apokteinai ephobēthē ton ochlon hoti hōs prophētēn auton eichon
verses.literal: Although Herod wanted to kill John he was afraid of the people because they regarded John as a prophet
verses.literalPt: E, querendo matá-lo, temia o povo; porque o tinham como profeta.

verses.original: Γενεσίοις δὲ γενομένοις τοῦ Ἡρῴδου ὠρχήσατο ἡ θυγάτηρ τῆς Ἡρῳδιάδος ἐν τῷ μέσῳ καὶ ἤρεσεν τῷ Ἡρῴδῃ
verses.transliteration: Genesiois de genomenois tou Hērōdou ōrchēsato hē thygatēr tēs Hērōdiados en tō mesō kai ēresen tō Hērōdē
verses.literal: On Herod’s birthday . . . however the daughter of Herodias danced before them . . . . . . and pleased Herod
verses.literalPt: Festejando-se, porém, o dia natalício de Herodes, dançou a filha de Herodias diante dele, e agradou a Herodes.

verses.original: ὅθεν μεθ’ ὅρκου ὡμολόγησεν αὐτῇ δοῦναι ὃ ἐὰν αἰτήσηται
verses.transliteration: hothen meth’ horkou hōmologēsen autē dounai ho ean aitēsētai
verses.literal: so much that he promised with an oath to give to her whatever . . . she asked
verses.literalPt: Por isso prometeu, com juramento, dar-lhe tudo o que pedisse;

verses.original: Ἡ δὲ προβιβασθεῖσα ὑπὸ τῆς μητρὸς αὐτῆς Δός μοι φησίν Ὧδε ἐπὶ πίνακι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ Βαπτιστοῦ
verses.transliteration: Hē de probibastheisa hypo tēs mētros autēs Dos moi phēsin Hōde epi pinaki tēn kephalēn Iōannou tou Baptistou
verses.literal: Prompted by her mother she said Give me here on a platter the head of John the Baptist
verses.literalPt: E ela, instruída previamente por sua mãe, disse: Dá-me aqui, num prato, a cabeça de João o Batista.

verses.original: Καὶ λυπηθεὶς ὁ βασιλεὺς διὰ τοὺς ὅρκους καὶ τοὺς συνανακειμένους ἐκέλευσεν δοθῆναι
verses.transliteration: Kai lypētheis ho basileus dia tous horkous kai tous synanakeimenous ekeleusen dothēnai
verses.literal: The king was grieved but because of his oaths and his guests he ordered that her wish be granted
verses.literalPt: E o rei afligiu-se, mas, por causa do juramento, e dos que estavam à mesa com ele, ordenou que se lhe desse.

verses.original: καὶ πέμψας ἀπεκεφάλισεν τὸν Ἰωάννην ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ
verses.transliteration: kai pempsas apekephalisen ton Iōannēn en tē phylakē
verses.literal: and sent to have John beheaded in the prison
verses.literalPt: E mandou degolar João no cárcere.

verses.original: Καὶ ἠνέχθη ἡ κεφαλὴ αὐτοῦ ἐπὶ πίνακι καὶ ἐδόθη τῷ κορασίῳ καὶ ἤνεγκεν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτῆς
verses.transliteration: Kai ēnechthē hē kephalē autou epi pinaki kai edothē tō korasiō kai ēnenken tē mētri autēs
verses.literal: John’s head was brought in on a platter and presented to the girl who carried it to her mother
verses.literalPt: E a sua cabeça foi trazida num prato, e dada à jovem, e ela a levou a sua mãe.

verses.original: καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ἦραν τὸ πτῶμα καὶ ἔθαψαν αὐτόν καὶ ἐλθόντες ἀπήγγειλαν τῷ Ἰησοῦ
verses.transliteration: kai proselthontes hoi mathētai autou ēran to ptōma kai ethapsan auton kai elthontes apēngeilan tō Iēsou
verses.literal: Then John’s disciples came and took his body and buried it And they went and informed Jesus
verses.literalPt: E chegaram os seus discípulos, e levaram o corpo, e o sepultaram; e foram anunciá-lo a Jesus.

verses.original: Ἀκούσας δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἀνεχώρησεν ἐκεῖθεν ἐν πλοίῳ εἰς ἔρημον τόπον κατ’ ἰδίαν καὶ ἀκούσαντες οἱ ὄχλοι ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ πεζῇ ἀπὸ τῶν πόλεων
verses.transliteration: Akousas de ho Iēsous anechōrēsen ekeithen en ploiō eis erēmon topon kat’ idian kai akousantes hoi ochloi ēkolouthēsan autō pezē apo tōn poleōn
verses.literal: When Jesus heard about John He withdrew . . . by boat privately to a solitary place But the crowds found out about it and followed Him on foot from the towns
verses.literalPt: E Jesus, ouvindo isto, retirou-se dali num barco, para um lugar deserto, apartado; e, sabendo-o o povo, seguiu-o a pé desde as cidades.

verses.original: Καὶ ἐξελθὼν εἶδεν πολὺν ὄχλον καὶ ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπ’ αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐθεράπευσεν τοὺς ἀρρώστους αὐτῶν
verses.transliteration: Kai exelthōn eiden polyn ochlon kai esplanchnisthē ep’ autois kai etherapeusen tous arrōstous autōn
verses.literal: When He stepped ashore and saw a large crowd He had compassion on them and healed their sick
verses.literalPt: E, Jesus, saindo, viu uma grande multidão, e possuído de íntima compaixão para com ela, curou os seus enfermos.

verses.original: Ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης προσῆλθον αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ λέγοντες Ἔρημός ἐστιν ὁ τόπος καὶ ἡ ὥρα ἤδη παρῆλθεν ἀπόλυσον οὖν τοὺς ὄχλους ἵνα ἀπελθόντες εἰς τὰς κώμας ἀγοράσωσιν ἑαυτοῖς βρώματα
verses.transliteration: Opsias de genomenēs prosēlthon autō hoi mathētai legontes Erēmos estin ho topos kai hē hōra ēdē parēlthen apolyson oun tous ochlous hina apelthontes eis tas kōmas agorasōsin heautois brōmata
verses.literal: When evening came the disciples came to Him and said This is a desolate place and the hour is already late . . . Dismiss the crowds so they can go to the villages and buy themselves some food
verses.literalPt: E, sendo chegada a tarde, os seus discípulos aproximaram-se dele, dizendo: O lugar é deserto, e a hora é já avançada; despede a multidão, para que vão pelas aldeias, e comprem comida para si.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν ἀπελθεῖν δότε αὐτοῖς ὑμεῖς φαγεῖν
verses.transliteration: Ho de Iēsous eipen autois Ou chreian echousin apelthein dote autois hymeis phagein
verses.literal: They do not need to go away - Jesus replied You give them something to eat
verses.literalPt: Jesus, porém, lhes disse: Não é mister que vão; dai-lhes vós de comer.

verses.original: Οἱ δὲ λέγουσιν αὐτῷ Οὐκ ἔχομεν ὧδε εἰ μὴ πέντε ἄρτους καὶ δύο ἰχθύας
verses.transliteration: Hoi de legousin autō Ouk echomen hōde ei mē pente artous kai dyo ichthyas
verses.literal: We have here only . . . five loaves of bread and two fish - they answered
verses.literalPt: Então eles lhe disseram: Não temos aqui senão cinco pães e dois peixes.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Φέρετέ μοι ὧδε αὐτούς
verses.transliteration: Ho de eipen Pherete moi hōde autous
verses.literal: Bring them here to Me - Jesus said
verses.literalPt: E ele disse: Trazei-mos aqui.

verses.original: καὶ κελεύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνακλιθῆναι ἐπὶ τοῦ χόρτου λαβὼν τοὺς πέντε ἄρτους καὶ τοὺς δύο ἰχθύας ἀναβλέψας εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εὐλόγησεν καὶ κλάσας ἔδωκεν τοῖς μαθηταῖς τοὺς ἄρτους οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ τοῖς ὄχλοις
verses.transliteration: kai keleusas tous ochlous anaklithēnai epi tou chortou labōn tous pente artous kai tous dyo ichthyas anablepsas eis ton ouranon eulogēsen kai klasas edōken tois mathētais tous artous hoi de mathētai tois ochlois
verses.literal: And He directed the crowds to sit down on the grass Taking the five loaves and the two fish and looking up to heaven He spoke a blessing Then He broke the loaves and gave them to the disciples and the disciples gave them to the people
verses.literalPt: E, tendo mandado que a multidão se assentasse sobre a erva, tomou os cinco pães e os dois peixes, e, erguendo os olhos ao céu, os abençoou, e, partindo os pães, deu-os aos discípulos, e os discípulos à multidão.

verses.original: Καὶ ἔφαγον πάντες καὶ ἐχορτάσθησαν καὶ ἦραν τὸ περισσεῦον τῶν κλασμάτων δώδεκα κοφίνους πλήρεις
verses.transliteration: Kai ephagon pantes kai echortasthēsan kai ēran to perisseuon tōn klasmatōn dōdeka kophinous plēreis
verses.literal: They all ate and were satisfied and the disciples picked up twelve basketfuls . . . of broken pieces that were left over
verses.literalPt: E comeram todos, e saciaram-se; e levantaram dos pedaços, que sobejaram, doze alcofas cheias.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἐσθίοντες ἦσαν ἄνδρες ὡσεὶ πεντακισχίλιοι χωρὶς γυναικῶν καὶ παιδίων
verses.transliteration: hoi de esthiontes ēsan andres hōsei pentakischilioi chōris gynaikōn kai paidiōn
verses.literal: About five thousand men were fed besides women and children
verses.literalPt: E os que comeram foram quase cinco mil homens, além das mulheres e crianças.

verses.original: Καὶ εὐθέως ἠνάγκασεν τοὺς μαθητὰς ἐμβῆναι εἰς τὸ πλοῖον καὶ προάγειν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸ πέραν ἕως οὗ ἀπολύσῃ τοὺς ὄχλους
verses.transliteration: Kai eutheōs ēnankasen tous mathētas embēnai eis to ploion kai proagein auton eis to peran heōs hou apolysē tous ochlous
verses.literal: Immediately Jesus made the disciples get into . . . the boat and go on ahead of Him to the other side while . . . He dismissed the crowds
verses.literalPt: E logo ordenou Jesus que os seus discípulos entrassem no barco, e fossem adiante para o outro lado, enquanto despedia a multidão.

verses.original: καὶ ἀπολύσας τοὺς ὄχλους ἀνέβη εἰς τὸ ὄρος κατ’ ἰδίαν προσεύξασθαι ὀψίας δὲ γενομένης μόνος ἦν ἐκεῖ
verses.transliteration: kai apolysas tous ochlous anebē eis to oros kat’ idian proseuxasthai opsias de genomenēs monos ēn ekei
verses.literal: After He had dismissed them . . . . . . He went up on the mountain by Himself to pray When evening came He was there alone
verses.literalPt: E, despedida a multidão, subiu ao monte para orar, à parte. E, chegada já a tarde, estava ali só.

verses.original: τὸ δὲ πλοῖον ἤδη σταδίους πολλοὺς ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἀπεῖχεν βασανιζόμενον ὑπὸ τῶν κυμάτων ἦν γὰρ ἐναντίος ὁ ἄνεμος
verses.transliteration: to de ploion ēdē stadious pollous apo tēs gēs apeichen basanizomenon hypo tōn kymatōn ēn gar enantios ho anemos
verses.literal: but the boat was already far . . . from land buffeted by the waves because the wind was against it
verses.literalPt: E o barco estava já no meio do mar, açoitado pelas ondas; porque o vento era contrário;

verses.original: Τετάρτῃ δὲ φυλακῇ τῆς νυκτὸς ἦλθεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς περιπατῶν ἐπὶ τὴν θάλασσαν
verses.transliteration: Tetartē de phylakē tēs nyktos ēlthen pros autous peripatōn epi tēn thalassan
verses.literal: During the fourth watch of the night Jesus went out to them walking on the sea
verses.literalPt: Mas, à quarta vigília da noite, dirigiu-se Jesus para eles, andando por cima do mar.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ μαθηταὶ ἰδόντες αὐτὸν ἐπὶ τῆς θαλάσσης περιπατοῦντα ἐταράχθησαν λέγοντες ὅτι Φάντασμά ἐστιν καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ φόβου ἔκραξαν
verses.transliteration: hoi de mathētai idontes auton epi tēs thalassēs peripatounta etarachthēsan legontes hoti Phantasma estin kai apo tou phobou ekraxan
verses.literal: When the disciples saw Him walking on the sea they were terrified It’s a ghost they said and cried out in fear
verses.literalPt: E os discípulos, vendo-o andando sobre o mar, assustaram-se, dizendo: É um fantasma. E gritaram com medo.

verses.original: Εὐθὺς δὲ ἐλάλησεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς αὐτοῖς λέγων Θαρσεῖτε ἐγώ εἰμι μὴ φοβεῖσθε
verses.transliteration: Euthys de elalēsen ho Iēsous autois legōn Tharseite egō eimi mē phobeisthe
verses.literal: But Jesus spoke up . . . at once - Take courage It is I Do not be afraid
verses.literalPt: Jesus, porém, lhes falou logo, dizendo: Tende bom ânimo, sou eu, não temais.

verses.original: Ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος εἶπεν Κύριε εἰ σὺ εἶ κέλευσόν με ἐλθεῖν πρὸς σὲ ἐπὶ τὰ ὕδατα
verses.transliteration: Apokritheis de autō ho Petros eipen Kyrie ei sy ei keleuson me elthein pros se epi ta hydata
verses.literal: Lord if it is You Peter replied . . . . . . . . . command me to come to You on the water
verses.literalPt: E respondeu-lhe Pedro, e disse: Senhor, se és tu, manda-me ir ter contigo por cima das águas.

verses.original: Ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ἐλθέ Καὶ καταβὰς ἀπὸ τοῦ πλοίου ὁ Πέτρος περιεπάτησεν ἐπὶ τὰ ὕδατα καὶ ἦλθεν πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν
verses.transliteration: Ho de eipen Elthe Kai katabas apo tou ploiou ho Petros periepatēsen epi ta hydata kai ēlthen pros ton Iēsoun
verses.literal: Come said Jesus Then Peter got down out of the boat walked on the water and came toward Jesus
verses.literalPt: E ele disse: Vem. E Pedro, descendo do barco, andou sobre as águas para ir ter com Jesus.

verses.original: βλέπων δὲ τὸν ἄνεμον ἰσχυρὸν ἐφοβήθη καὶ ἀρξάμενος καταποντίζεσθαι ἔκραξεν λέγων Κύριε σῶσόν με
verses.transliteration: blepōn de ton anemon ischyron ephobēthē kai arxamenos katapontizesthai ekraxen legōn Kyrie sōson me
verses.literal: But when he saw the strength of the wind he was afraid and beginning to sink cried out Lord save me
verses.literalPt: Mas, sentindo o vento forte, teve medo; e, começando a ir para o fundo, clamou, dizendo: Senhor, salva-me!

verses.original: Εὐθέως δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἐπελάβετο αὐτοῦ καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ Ὀλιγόπιστε εἰς τί ἐδίστασας
verses.transliteration: Eutheōs de ho Iēsous ekteinas tēn cheira epelabeto autou kai legei autō Oligopiste eis ti edistasas
verses.literal: Immediately Jesus reached out His hand and took hold of Peter You of little faith He said why . . . did you doubt
verses.literalPt: E logo Jesus, estendendo a mão, segurou-o, e disse-lhe: Homem de pouca fé, por que duvidaste?

verses.original: Καὶ ἀναβάντων αὐτῶν εἰς τὸ πλοῖον ἐκόπασεν ὁ ἄνεμος
verses.transliteration: Kai anabantōn autōn eis to ploion ekopasen ho anemos
verses.literal: And when they had climbed back into the boat the wind died down
verses.literalPt: E, quando subiram para o barco, acalmou o vento.

verses.original: οἱ δὲ ἐν τῷ πλοίῳ προσεκύνησαν αὐτῷ λέγοντες Ἀληθῶς Θεοῦ Υἱὸς εἶ
verses.transliteration: hoi de en tō ploiō prosekynēsan autō legontes Alēthōs Theou Huios ei
verses.literal: Then those who were in the boat worshiped Him saying Truly You are the Son of God
verses.literalPt: Então aproximaram-se os que estavam no barco, e adoraram-no, dizendo: És verdadeiramente o Filho de Deus.

verses.original: Καὶ διαπεράσαντες ἦλθον ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν εἰς Γεννησαρέτ
verses.transliteration: Kai diaperasantes ēlthon epi tēn gēn eis Gennēsaret
verses.literal: When they had crossed over they landed . . . . . . . . . at Gennesaret
verses.literalPt: E, tendo passado para o outro lado, chegaram à terra de Genesaré.

verses.original: καὶ ἐπιγνόντες αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες τοῦ τόπου ἐκείνου ἀπέστειλαν εἰς ὅλην τὴν περίχωρον ἐκείνην καὶ προσήνεγκαν αὐτῷ πάντας τοὺς κακῶς ἔχοντας
verses.transliteration: kai epignontes auton hoi andres tou topou ekeinou apesteilan eis holēn tēn perichōron ekeinēn kai prosēnenkan autō pantas tous kakōs echontas
verses.literal: And when the men of that place recognized Jesus they sent word to all the surrounding region People brought all the sick to Him
verses.literalPt: E, quando os homens daquele lugar o conheceram, mandaram por todas aquelas terras em redor e trouxeram-lhe todos os que estavam enfermos.

verses.original: καὶ παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν ἵνα μόνον ἅψωνται τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ καὶ ὅσοι ἥψαντο διεσώθησαν
verses.transliteration: kai parekaloun auton hina monon hapsōntai tou kraspedou tou himatiou autou kai hosoi hēpsanto diesōthēsan
verses.literal: and begged Him just to let them touch the fringe of His cloak And all who touched Him were healed
verses.literalPt: E rogavam-lhe que ao menos eles pudessem tocar a orla da sua roupa; e todos os que a tocavam ficavam sãos.
